title: Beyond the 956: Randall England, 'General Hospital' villain Jack Slater, dies at 75
excerpt: Randall England, the actor best known as villain Jack Slater on "General Hospital" in the 1980s, died September 25, 2026, after a battle with esophageal cancer. He was 75.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Randall England, the actor best known as the villain Jack Slater on the soap opera General Hospital, has died at 75.

England died September 25, 2026, after a battle with esophageal cancer. According to his family's obituary, he passed away peacefully, surrounded by loved ones. Deadline first reported his death on November 11, and USA TODAY, Page Six and TMZ also reported it.

Born Randy Alan England in Oklahoma City, he graduated from the University of Oklahoma and moved to New York City to pursue modeling, appearing in advertising campaigns for Viceroy cigarettes, Dunlop tires, Michelob and PlayStation. He began acting in the late 1970s and later moved to Los Angeles, where he lived in Beverly Hills for more than 40 years.

He became a familiar face to soap opera fans in the 1980s as Jack Slater, a criminal and jewel thief known for his signature cowboy boots, on General Hospital. He appeared in 31 episodes from 1984 to 1985, before his character was killed in a shootout.

His other credits included Dallas, The Young and the Restless, Baywatch and Beverly Hills Chihuahua, as well as Maroon 5's "Sugar" music video. His stage work included productions of All My Sons, The Glass Menagerie and Anton Chekhov's The Three Sisters, which earned a Drama-Logue Award for best ensemble cast in 1994. He was also a composer and music producer who created work under the name RAE.

England is survived by his daughter, Micaela Reed; his son-in-law, Sam Reed; his grandchildren, Katherine and Julian Reed; his mother, Catherine Burgess; and his sister, Linda Baker. Donations in his memory can be made to the Esophageal Cancer Action Network.

Rest in Peace, Randall England.

Sources: Deadline; USA TODAY; Page Six; TMZ.
